title.zh: 卷十七 列傳第十一 王珍國 馬仙琕 張齊
title.en: Volume 17: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi
title.raw: 卷十七 列傳第十一 王珍國 馬仙琕 張齊 Volume 17: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十七 列傳第十一

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 17, Biographies 11
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 17, Biographies 11

sentences.zh: 王珍國 馬仙琕 張齊

translations.literal: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenguo; Ma Xianpin; Zhang Qi

sentences.zh: 王珍國字德重，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenguo, styled Dezong, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenguo, styled Dezong, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父廣之，齊世良將，官至散騎常侍、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Guangzhi was a fine general of Qi, reaching scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and chariot-and-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangzhi was a noted Qi general who rose to scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and chariot-and-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 珍國起家冠軍行參軍，累遷虎賁中郎將、南譙太守，治有能名。

translations.literal: Zhenguo began office as champion army acting staff officer, rose through tiger-guard commandant of the center and Nanqiao prefect, and was famed for capable governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo began as champion army acting staff officer, rose through tiger-guard commandant of the center and Nanqiao prefect, and won a name for able rule.

sentences.zh: 時郡境苦饑，乃發米散財，以拯窮乏。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery suffered bitter famine; he issued grain and scattered wealth to relieve the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was in bitter famine; he opened granaries and scattered wealth to save the poor.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝手敕云：「卿愛人治國，甚副吾意也。

translations.literal: Qi Gaodi wrote by hand: "You love the people and govern the state well—this suits my intent very well.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Gaodi wrote by hand, "You love the people and govern the state—this suits my intent well.

sentences.zh: 」永明初，遷桂陽內史，討捕盜賊，境內肅清。

translations.literal: " At the start of Yongming he was transferred to Guiyang interior governor, hunted down bandits and robbers, and the territory was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: " At the start of Yongming he became Guiyang interior governor, hunted bandits, and pacified the territory.

sentences.zh: 罷任還都，路經江州，刺史柳世隆臨渚餞別，見珍國還裝輕素，乃歎曰：「此真可謂良二千石也！

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital; passing through Jiangzhou, Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to bid farewell, saw Zhenguo's return baggage light and plain, and sighed: "This truly may be called a fine two-thousand-dan official!
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court; passing Jiangzhou, Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to see him off, saw his baggage light and plain, and sighed, "This is a true two-thousand-dan official!

sentences.zh: 」還爲大司馬中兵參軍。

translations.literal: " On return he was made grand marshal central army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: " On return he was made grand marshal central army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 武帝雅相知賞，每歎曰：「晚代將家子弟，有如珍國者少矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi greatly knew and appreciated him; he often sighed and said: "Among later-age generals' sons, few are like Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi knew and prized him; he often sighed and said, "Among later generations of generals' houses, few sons are like Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 」復出爲安成內史。

translations.literal: " He went out again as Ancheng interior governor.
translations.idiomatic: " He went out again as Ancheng interior governor.

sentences.zh: 入爲越騎校尉，冠軍長史、鐘離太守。

translations.literal: He entered office as crossbow-and-horses commandant, champion chief of staff, and Zhongli prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as crossbow-and-horses commandant, champion chief of staff, and Zhongli prefect.

sentences.zh: 仍遷巴東、建平二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to prefect of Ba and Ping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to prefect of Ba and Ping.

sentences.zh: 還爲遊擊將軍，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: On return he was made raid general and left office for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made raid general and left office for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 建武末，魏軍圍司州，明帝使徐州刺史裴叔業攻拔渦陽，以爲聲援，起珍國爲輔國將軍，率兵助焉。

translations.literal: Late in Jianwu, Wei forces besieged Si Province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye to attack and capture Guoyang as a diversion, and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to lead troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu, Wei besieged Si province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou inspector Pei Shuye to take Guoyang as a diversion and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 魏將楊大眼大衆奄至，叔業懼，棄軍走，珍國率其衆殿，故不至大敗。

translations.literal: Wei general Yang Dayan's great host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led his men as rearguard, so they did not suffer great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei general Yang Dayan's host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led the rearguard, so the defeat was not total.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，會稽太守王敬則反，珍國又率衆距之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year one, Kuaiji prefect Wang Jingze rebelled; Zhenguo again led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 敬則平，遷寧朔將軍、青、冀二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze was pacified, he was made pacifying-the-north general and inspector of Qing and Ji, general as before.

sentences.zh: 義師起，東昏召珍國以衆還京師，入頓建康城。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, Donghun summoned Zhenguo with his troops back to the capital; he entered and garrisoned Jiankang city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army rose, Donghun summoned Zhenguo with his troops to the capital; he entered and garrisoned Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 義師至，使珍國出屯朱雀門，爲王茂軍所敗，乃入城。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army arrived, Donghun had Zhenguo go out and camp at Zhuque Gate; he was defeated by Wang Mao's army and re-entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army arrived, Donghun sent Zhenguo to camp at Zhuque Gate; Wang Mao's army defeated him and he re-entered the city.

sentences.zh: 仍密遣郄纂奉明鏡獻誠於高祖，高祖斷金以報之。

translations.literal: He then secretly sent Xi Zuan to present a bright mirror as pledge of loyalty to Gaozu; Gaozu broke gold to answer him.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent Xi Zuan to present a bright mirror to Gaozu as pledge of loyalty; Gaozu broke gold in answer.

sentences.zh: 時城中咸思從義，莫敢先發，侍中、衛尉張稷都督衆軍，珍國潛結稷腹心張齊要稷，稷許之。

translations.literal: At the time everyone in the city wished to follow righteousness, yet none dared act first; Attendant Zhang Ji as Ministry of Guard general commanded all troops; Zhenguo secretly joined with Ji's trusted man Zhang Qi to win Ji over, and Ji agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city wished to turn to the righteous cause, yet none dared move first; attendant Zhang Ji as Ministry of Guard general commanded the host; Zhenguo secretly won over Ji's confidant Zhang Qi to sway Ji, and Ji agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅旦，珍國引稷於衛尉府，勒兵入自雲龍門，卽東昏於內殿斬之，與稷會尚書僕射王亮等於西鐘下，使中書舍人裴長穆等奉東昏首歸高祖。

translations.literal: On the morning of day bingyin in the twelfth month, Zhenguo led Ji to the Ministry of Guard headquarters, mustered troops entering by Cloud Dragon Gate, and at once beheaded Donghun in the inner hall; with Ji he met Right Vice Director Wang Liang and others below the western bell, and had Palace Scribe-in-Ordinary Pei Changmu and others present Donghun's head to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of day bingyin in the twelfth month, Zhenguo led Ji to the Ministry of Guard headquarters, mustered troops through Cloud Dragon Gate, and at once beheaded Donghun in the inner hall; with Ji he met right vice director Wang Liang and others below the western bell and had palace scribe Pei Changmu and others present Donghun's head to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 以功授右衛將軍，辭不拜；

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed right guard general; he declined and did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was appointed right guard general; he declined;

sentences.zh: 又授徐州刺史，固乞留京師。

translations.literal: Again appointed Xuzhou inspector; he firmly begged to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Again appointed Xuzhou inspector; he firmly begged to stay in the capital.

sentences.zh: 復賜金帛，珍國又固讓。

translations.literal: Again granted gold and silk; Zhenguo again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Again granted gold and silk; Zhenguo again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 敕答曰：「昔田子泰固辭絹穀。

translations.literal: Edict replied: "In old times Tian Zitai firmly declined silk and grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "In old times Tian Zitai firmly declined silk and grain.

sentences.zh: 卿體國情深，良在可嘉。

translations.literal: Your care for the state runs deep—truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Your care for the state runs deep—truly praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 」後因侍宴，帝問曰：「卿明鏡尚存，昔金何在？

translations.literal: " Later at a feast the emperor asked: "Your bright mirror still exists—where is the gold of old?
translations.idiomatic: " Later at a feast the emperor asked, "Your bright mirror still exists—where is the gold of old?

sentences.zh: 」珍國答曰：「黃金謹在臣肘，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: " Zhenguo answered: "The gold is carefully at my elbow; I dare not let it fall."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenguo answered, "The gold is carefully at my elbow; I dare not let it fall."

sentences.zh: 」復爲右衛將軍，加給事中，遷左衛將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Again made right guard general, with additional supervisory attendant; transferred to left guard general with additional scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Again made right guard general with additional supervisory attendant; transferred to left guard general with additional scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 天監初，封灄陽縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhenyang with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除都官尚書，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Made Director of the Court for Public Works, attendant-in-ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Made director of the court for public works, attendant-in-ordinary as before.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏任城王元澄寇鐘離，高祖遣珍國，因問討賊方略。

translations.literal: In year five, Wei's Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng raided Zhongli; Gaozu sent Zhenguo and asked the strategy for attacking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, Wei's prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng raided Zhongli; Gaozu sent Zhenguo and asked how to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 珍國對曰：「臣常患魏衆少，不苦其多。

translations.literal: Zhenguo replied: "Your subject always worries that Wei has too few troops, not that they have too many."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo replied, "Your subject always worries that Wei has too few troops, not that they have too many."

sentences.zh: 」高祖壯其言，乃假節，與衆軍同討焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu admired his words and then granted credentials of office; he joined the armies in the campaign together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu admired his words, granted credentials, and sent him with the armies on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，班師。

translations.literal: Wei forces withdrew; the army returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Wei withdrew; the army returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 出爲使持節、都督梁秦二州諸軍事、征虜將軍、南秦梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as bearer of staff and credentials, commander of military affairs in Liang and Qin, campaign general who subdues barbarians, and inspector of Nan and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearer of staff, commander of Liang and Qin military affairs, campaign general who subdues barbarians, and inspector of Nan and Liang.

sentences.zh: 會梁州長史夏侯道遷以州降魏，珍國步道出魏興，將襲之，不果，遂留鎮焉。

translations.literal: When Liang's long chief of staff Xia Hou Daoyuan surrendered the province to Wei, Zhenguo marched by land through Wei Xing intending to strike, but did not succeed, and remained to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's long chief of staff Xia Hou Daoyuan surrendered the province to Wei, Zhenguo marched overland through Wei Xing to strike but failed and remained to garrison.

sentences.zh: 以無功，累表請解，高祖弗許。

translations.literal: For lack of merit he repeatedly memorialized to resign; Gaozu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: For lack of merit he repeatedly asked to resign; Gaozu would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 改封宜陽縣侯，戶邑如前。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yiyang, fief households as before.
translations.idiomatic: His enfeoffment was changed to marquis of Yiyang, households as before.

sentences.zh: 徵還爲員外散騎常侍、太子右衛率，加後軍。

translations.literal: Recalled to be outer scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and crown prince right guard leader, with additional rear army.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as outer scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and crown prince right guard leader, with additional rear army.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復爲左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, again left guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, again left guard general.

sentences.zh: 九年，出爲使持節、都督湘州諸軍事、信武將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In year nine he went out as bearer of staff, commander of Xiang military affairs, faithful martial general, and Xiang inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he went out bearer of staff, commander of Xiang military affairs, faithful martial general, and Xiang inspector.

sentences.zh: 視事四年，徵還爲護軍將軍，遷通直散騎常侍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was recalled as Protector General, transferred to undisguised scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and Danyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office he was recalled as protector general, then undisguised scattered-cavalry attendant-in-ordinary and Danyang governor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈車騎將軍，給鼓吹一部，賻錢十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: Edict granted chariot-and-cavalry general, one set of martial music, funeral money ten thousand, and cloth one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted chariot-and-cavalry general, one set of martial music, ten thousand cash for the funeral, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Wei.

sentences.zh: 子僧度嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sengdu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengdu inherited.

sentences.zh: 馬仙琕，字靈馥，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xianpin, styled Lingfu, came from Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父伯鸞，宋冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Boluan was Song champion army acting chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boluan was Song champion army acting chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 仙琕少以果敢聞，遭父憂，毀瘠過禮，負土成墳，手植松柏。

translations.literal: Xianpin from youth was known for daring and resolve; when his father died his grief-wasting exceeded ritual—he carried earth to make the mound and planted pines and cypresses with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xianpin was known for daring; when his father died his mourning exceeded ritual—he carried earth for the mound and planted pines and cypresses himself.

sentences.zh: 起家郢州主簿，遷武騎常侍，爲小將，隨齊安陸王蕭緬。

translations.literal: He began office as Yezhou chief clerk, transferred to martial-cavalry regular attendant, served as a junior officer, and followed Qi Prince of Anlu Xiao Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Yezhou chief clerk, rose to martial-cavalry regular attendant, served as a junior officer, and followed Qi's prince of Anlu Xiao Mian.

sentences.zh: 緬卒，事明帝。

translations.literal: When Mian died, he served Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian died, he served Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 永元中，蕭遙光、崔慧景亂，累有戰功，以勳至前將軍。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan, Xiao Yaoguang and Cui Huijing rebelled; he repeatedly had battle merit and through merit rose to front general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan, Xiao Yaoguang and Cui Huijing rebelled; he won repeated battle merit and rose to front general.

sentences.zh: 出爲龍驤將軍、南汝陰、譙二郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as dragon-prancing general and prefect of Nan Ruyin and Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as dragon-prancing general and prefect of Nan Ruyin and Qiao.

sentences.zh: 會壽陽新陷，魏將王肅侵邊，仙琕力戰，以寡克衆，魏人甚憚之。

translations.literal: When Shouchun had newly fallen, Wei general Wang Su invaded the border; Xianpin fought hard, with the few overcame the many, and Wei men greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun had newly fallen, Wei general Wang Su raided the border; Xianpin fought hard, the few overcame the many, and Wei greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 復以功遷寧朔將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Again through merit he was transferred to pacifying-the-north general and Yuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Again through merit he was transferred to pacifying-the-north general and Yuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 義師起，四方多回應，高祖使仙琕故人姚仲賓說之，仙琕於軍斬仲賓以徇。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, all quarters largely responded; Gaozu sent Xianpin's old friend Yao Zhongbin to persuade him; Xianpin in the army beheaded Zhongbin to display to the host.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army rose, all quarters largely responded; Gaozu sent Xianpin's old friend Yao Zhongbin to win him over; Xianpin beheaded Zhongbin in camp to warn the host.

sentences.zh: 義師至新林，仙琕猶持兵於江西，日鈔運漕，建康城陷，仙琕號哭經宿，乃解兵歸罪。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, Xianpin still held arms on the west of the river, daily requisitioning transport grain; when Jiankang fell, Xianpin wept and wailed a whole night, then laid down arms and came to submit his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army reached Xinlin, Xianpin still held arms west of the river, daily requisitioning transport grain; when Jiankang fell, he wept all night, then laid down arms and came to submit his guilt.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「射鉤斬袪，昔人弗忌。

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Shooting the hook, cutting the sleeve—men of old did not resent such.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu comforted him, saying, "Shooting the hook, cutting the sleeve—men of old did not resent such things.

sentences.zh: 卿勿以戮使斷運，苟自嫌絕也。

translations.literal: Do not, because you killed the envoy and cut off supply, needlessly estrange yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Do not, because you killed the envoy and cut off supply, needlessly estrange yourself."

sentences.zh: 」仙琕謝曰：「小人如失主犬，後主飼之，便復爲用。

translations.literal: Xianpin apologized: "A petty man is like a stray dog without a master; when a new master feeds it, it will serve again."
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin apologized, "A petty man is like a stray dog without a master; when a new master feeds it, it serves again."

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑而美之。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and praised him.

sentences.zh: 俄而仙琕母卒，高祖知其貧，賻給甚厚。

translations.literal: Soon Xianpin's mother died; Gaozu knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianpin's mother died; Gaozu knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.

sentences.zh: 仙琕號泣，謂弟仲艾曰：「蒙大造之恩，未獲上報。

translations.literal: Xianpin wept and said to his younger brother Zhong'ai: "Having received great creating grace, I have not yet repaid it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin wept and said to his younger brother Zhong'ai, "Having received great creating grace, I have not yet repaid it.

sentences.zh: 今復荷殊澤，當與爾以心力自效耳。」

translations.literal: Now again receiving special favor—we shall repay with all our strength, you and I."
translations.idiomatic: Now again receiving special favor—we shall repay with all our strength, you and I."

sentences.zh: 天監四年，王師北討，仙琕每戰，勇冠三軍，當其沖者，莫不摧破。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year four, the royal army marched north; Xianpin in every battle was bravest in the three armies; whoever met his charge was not left unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year four, the royal army marched north; Xianpin in every battle was bravest in the three armies; whoever met his charge was shattered.

sentences.zh: 與諸將論議，口未嘗言功。

translations.literal: When discussing with the generals, he never spoke of merit in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals discussed affairs, he never spoke of merit.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，仙琕曰：「丈夫爲時所知，當進不求名，退不逃罪，乃平生願也。

translations.literal: When asked the reason, Xianpin said: "A man whom the age knows should advance without seeking fame and retreat without escaping punishment—that is his lifetime wish.
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Xianpin said, "A man whom the age knows should advance without seeking fame and retreat without escaping punishment—that is his lifetime wish.

sentences.zh: 何功可論！

translations.literal: What merit is there to discuss!
translations.idiomatic: What merit is there to discuss!

sentences.zh: 」授輔國將軍、宋安、安蠻二郡太守，遷南義陽太守。

translations.literal: " He was appointed supporting-the-state general and prefect of Song'an and Anman, transferred to south Yiyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed supporting-the-state general and prefect of Song'an and Anman, then south Yiyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 累破山蠻，郡境清謐。

translations.literal: He repeatedly broke the mountain barbarians; the commandery borders were quiet and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly broke the mountain barbarians; the commandery was quiet and orderly.

sentences.zh: 以功封浛洭縣伯，邑四百戶，仍遷都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史，輔國將軍如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Hansui with four hundred households, and was then transferred to commander of Si military affairs and Si inspector, supporting-the-state general as before.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Hansui with four hundred households, then commander of Si military affairs and Si inspector, supporting-the-state general as before.

sentences.zh: 俄進號貞威將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to faithful martial general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to faithful martial general.

sentences.zh: 魏豫州人白皁生殺其刺史琅邪王司馬慶曾，自號平北將軍，推鄉人胡遜爲刺史，以懸瓠來降。

translations.literal: A man of Wei Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, killed his inspector Prince of Langye Sima Qingzeng, styled himself pacifying-the-north general, and pushed his fellow villager Hu Xun as inspector to offer Xuanhu in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Wei Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, killed his inspector the prince of Langye Sima Qingzeng, styled himself pacifying-the-north general, and pushed his fellow villager Hu Xun as inspector to offer Xuanhu in surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖使仙琕赴之，又遣直閤將軍武會超、馬廣率衆爲援。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Xianpin to go; he also sent direct-palace general Wu Huichao and Ma Guang with troops as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Xianpin; he also sent direct-palace general Wu Huichao and Ma Guang with troops as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 仙琕進頓楚王城，遣副將齊苟兒以兵二千助守懸瓠。

translations.literal: Xianpin advanced and encamped at Prince of Chu city, sent Deputy General Qi Gou'er with two thousand troops to help guard Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin advanced and encamped at Prince of Chu city and sent deputy general Qi Gou'er with two thousand men to help guard Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 魏中山王元英率衆十萬攻懸瓠，仙琕遣廣、會超等守三關。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying led a hundred thousand host to attack Xuanhu; Xianpin sent Guang, Huichao, and others to guard the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying led a hundred thousand men against Xuanhu; Xianpin sent Guang, Huichao, and others to guard the three passes.

sentences.zh: 十二月，英破懸瓠，執齊苟兒，遂進攻馬廣，又破廣，生擒之，送雒陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Ying captured Xuanhu, seized Qi Gou'er, then advanced to attack Ma Guang and again defeated Guang, capturing him alive and sending him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Ying took Xuanhu, seized Qi Gou'er, then attacked Ma Guang and defeated him, capturing him alive and sending him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 仙琕不能救。

translations.literal: Xianpin could not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin could not rescue.

sentences.zh: 會超等亦相次退散，魏軍遂進據三關。

translations.literal: Huichao and the others also in succession withdrew and dispersed; Wei forces then advanced to occupy the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Huichao and the others also withdrew in succession; Wei then advanced and held the three passes.

sentences.zh: 仙琕坐徵還，爲雲騎將軍。

translations.literal: Xianpin sat out the blame and was recalled, made cloud-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin was recalled for the failure and made cloud-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 出爲仁威司馬，府主豫章王轉號雲麾，復爲司馬，加振遠將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as benevolent prestige staff officer; when the lord of the manor Prince of Yuzhang changed title to cloud-banner, he again became staff officer with additional shaking-the-distant general.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as benevolent prestige staff officer; when the manor lord Prince of Yuzhang changed title to cloud-banner, he again became staff officer with additional shaking-the-distant general.

sentences.zh: 十年，朐山民殺琅邪太守劉晣，以城降魏，詔假仙琕節，討之。

translations.literal: In year ten, the people of Qushan killed Langye prefect Liu Xi and offered the city in surrender to Wei; an edict granted Xianpin credentials to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten the people of Qushan killed Langye prefect Liu Xi and surrendered the city to Wei; an edict granted Xianpin credentials to attack.

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史盧昶以衆十餘萬赴焉。

translations.literal: Wei Xuzhou Inspector Lu Chang came with a host of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuzhou inspector Lu Chang came with more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 仙琕與戰，累破之，昶遁走。

translations.literal: Xianpin fought him, repeatedly defeating him; Chang fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin fought him, repeatedly defeated him, and Chang fled.

sentences.zh: 仙琕縱兵乘之，魏衆免者十一二，收其兵糧牛馬器械，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Xianpin loosed troops to pursue; of Wei's host only one or two in ten escaped; grain, cattle, horses, and implements taken were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Xianpin loosed troops in pursuit; only one or two in ten of Wei's host escaped; grain, cattle, horses, and arms taken were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 振旅還京師，遷太子左衛率，進爵爲侯，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: The army returned to the capital in triumph; he was transferred crown prince left guard leader, advanced in rank to marquis, fief increased by six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned in triumph; he was transferred crown prince left guard leader, advanced to marquis, fief increased by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷持節、督豫北豫霍三州諸軍事、信武將軍、豫州刺史，領南汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In year eleven he was transferred bearer of staff, commander of Yu, north Yu, and Huo, faithful martial general and Yuzhou inspector, with concurrent Nan Ruyin prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he was transferred bearer of staff, commander of Yu, north Yu, and Huo, faithful martial general and Yuzhou inspector, with concurrent Nan Ruyin prefect.

sentences.zh: 初，仙琕幼名仙婢，及長，以「婢」名不典，乃以「玉」代「女」，因成「琕」云。

translations.literal: At first Xianpin's childhood name was Xianbi; when grown, because "bi" as a name was not proper, he replaced "woman" with "jade," thus making "Xianpin," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xianpin's childhood name was Xianbi; when grown, because "bi" as a name was not proper, he replaced the female radical with jade and made "Xianpin," it is said.

sentences.zh: 自爲將及居州郡，能與士卒同勞逸。

translations.literal: From serving as general and holding commanderies and prefectures, he could share hardship and ease with officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: As general and in commanderies and prefectures, he shared hardship and ease with officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 身衣不過布帛，所居無帷幕衾屏，行則飲食與廝養最下者同。

translations.literal: His body clothing was no more than plain cloth and silk; where he dwelt there were no curtains, quilts, or screens; on the march his food and drink were the same as the lowest groom.
translations.idiomatic: His clothing was no more than plain cloth and silk; his dwelling had no curtains, quilts, or screens; on the march he ate and drank with the lowest groom.

sentences.zh: 其在邊境，常單身潛入敵庭，伺知壁壘村落險要處所，故戰多克捷，士卒亦甘心爲之用，高祖雅愛仗之。

translations.literal: On the borders he often went alone in secret into enemy camps to reconnoiter walls, stockades, villages, and strategic points; hence battles were mostly victorious, and the soldiers too were willing to die for him; Gaozu deeply loved and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: On the borders he often went alone in secret into enemy camps to learn walls, stockades, villages, and passes; hence he mostly won battles, and the soldiers were willing to die for him; Gaozu deeply loved and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 在州四年，卒。

translations.literal: After four years in the province he died.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in the province he died.

sentences.zh: 贈左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Granted left guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Granted left guard general.

sentences.zh: 諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Gang.

sentences.zh: 子巖夫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yanfu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanfu inherited.

sentences.zh: 張齊字子響，馮翊郡人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi, styled Zixiang, was a native of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi, styled Zixiang, was a man of Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 世居橫桑，或云橫桑人也。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt at Hengsang; some say he was a man of Hengsang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Hengsang; some say he was native there.

sentences.zh: 少有膽氣。

translations.literal: From youth he had daring and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had courage and spirit.

sentences.zh: 初事荊府司馬垣歷生。

translations.literal: At first he served Jing prefecture Chief of Staff Yuan Lisheng.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Jing prefecture chief of staff Yuan Lisheng.

sentences.zh: 歷生酗酒，遇下嚴酷，不甚禮之。

translations.literal: Lisheng was given to drink; he was harsh toward subordinates and did not treat Qi with much courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Lisheng drank heavily and was harsh to subordinates; he showed Qi little courtesy.

sentences.zh: 歷生罷官歸，吳郡張稷爲荊府司馬，齊復從之，稷甚相知重，以爲心腹，雖家居細事，皆以任焉。

translations.literal: When Lisheng left office and returned home, Zhang Ji of Wu commandery became Jing prefecture Chief of Staff; Qi again followed him. Ji knew and valued him deeply, taking him as a trusted confidant—even household trifles were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lisheng left office, Zhang Ji of Wu became Jing chief of staff; Qi followed him again. Ji deeply trusted him as a confidant and even entrusted household matters to him.

sentences.zh: 齊盡心事稷，無所辭憚。

translations.literal: Qi served Ji with his whole heart and shirked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served Ji wholeheartedly and shrank from nothing.

sentences.zh: 隨稷歸京師。

translations.literal: He followed Ji back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ji back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 稷爲南兗州，又擢爲府中兵參軍，始委以軍旅。

translations.literal: When Ji was made South Yanzhou inspector, Qi was also promoted to Military Participation Officer on the prefecture staff and for the first time was entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji took South Yanzhou, Qi was promoted to military participation officer on the staff and first put in charge of troops.

sentences.zh: 齊永元中，義師起，東昏徵稷歸，都督宮城諸軍事，居尚書省。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era of Qi, the Righteous Army rose; Donghun summoned Ji back, made him Area Commander of all palace-city military affairs, and had him reside in the Masters of Writing complex.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongyuan, the righteous army rose; Donghun recalled Ji, made him commander of palace-city forces, and lodged him in the Masters of Writing complex.

sentences.zh: 義兵至，周邊漸急，齊日造王珍國，陰與定計。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, the siege around them grew pressing; Qi went daily to Wang Zhenguo and secretly settled plans with him.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous army drew near and the ring tightened, Qi visited Wang Zhenguo daily and secretly fixed their plan.

sentences.zh: 計定，夜引珍國就稷造膝，齊自執燭以成謀。

translations.literal: Once the plan was set, at night he led Zhenguo to Ji to join in deliberation knee to knee; Qi himself held the candle to complete the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was set, at night he brought Zhenguo to Ji for a knee-to-knee counsel; Qi himself held the candle while they plotted.

sentences.zh: 明旦，與稷、珍國卽東昏於內殿，齊手刃焉。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, together with Ji and Zhenguo, he seized Donghun in the inner hall; Qi himself struck him dead with his blade.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he, Ji, and Zhenguo seized Donghun in the inner hall; Qi himself killed him with his blade.

sentences.zh: 明年，高祖受禪，封齊安昌縣侯，邑五百戶，仍爲寧朔將軍、歷陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozu received the abdication; Qi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anchang county in Qi with a fief of five hundred households, and remained Pacification North General and Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Gaozu took the throne; Qi was made Marquis of Anchang with five hundred households, retaining pacification north general and Liyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 齊手不知書，目不識字，而在郡有清政，吏事甚脩。

translations.literal: Qi did not know writing by hand and could not read characters by sight, yet in his commandery he had pure governance and handled official business very well.
translations.idiomatic: Qi could neither write nor read, yet in office he ruled cleanly and managed affairs diligently.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，還爲虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was recalled and made Tiger-Fang Central Corps General.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two he returned as tiger-fang central corps general.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遷天門太守，寧朔將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before he took the appointment he was transferred to Administrator of Tianmen, his Pacification North General title remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking post he was made Tianmen administrator, keeping pacification north general.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏將王足寇巴、蜀，高祖以齊爲輔國將軍救蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wei general Wang Zu invaded Ba and Shu; Gaozu made Qi Assists-the-State General to rescue Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Wei general Wang Zu invaded Ba and Shu; Gaozu made Qi assists-the-state general to relieve Shu.

sentences.zh: 未至，足退走，齊進戍南安。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Zu withdrew; Qi advanced to garrison Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Zu had withdrawn; Qi advanced to hold Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，使齊置大劍、寒冢二戍，軍還益州。

translations.literal: In autumn of the seventh year Qi was ordered to set up two garrisons at Dajian and Hanzong; the army returned to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year seven he set garrisons at Dajian and Hanzong, then returned the army to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷武旅將軍、巴西太守，尋加征遠將軍。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Martial Array General and Administrator of Baxi, and soon was additionally made Pacifies-the-Distance General.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became martial array general and Baxi administrator, soon with added pacifies-the-distance general.

sentences.zh: 十年，郡人姚景和聚合蠻蜒，抄斷江路，攻破金井。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, a man of the commandery, Yao Jinghe, gathered Man tribes of Yan and cut the river road, breaking Jinjing.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Yao Jinghe of the commandery rallied Man of Yan, cut the river route, and stormed Jinjing.

sentences.zh: 齊討景和於平昌，破之。

translations.literal: Qi attacked Jinghe at Pingchang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi attacked Jinghe at Pingchang and broke him.

sentences.zh: 初，南鄭沒於魏，乃於益州西置南梁州。

translations.literal: Earlier Nanzheng had fallen to Wei; then South Liang province was established west of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Nanzheng had fallen to Wei, so South Liang province was set up west of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 州鎮草創，皆仰益州取足。

translations.literal: The provincial seat was newly founded and depended wholly on Yizhou for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The new provincial seat depended wholly on Yizhou for supplies.

sentences.zh: 齊上夷獠義租，得米二十萬斛。

translations.literal: Qi reported righteous tribute levies from Yi and Liao, obtaining two hundred thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Qi reported righteous tribute from the Yi and Liao, gaining two hundred thousand hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 又立臺傳，興冶鑄，以應贍南梁。

translations.literal: He also set up relay stations and opened smelting and casting to supply South Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He also set relays and opened foundries to sustain South Liang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進假節、督益州外水諸軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to Acting Credentials and Area Commander of all Yizhou outer-water forces.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he gained acting credentials and command of Yizhou outer-water forces.

sentences.zh: 十二年，魏將傅豎眼寇南安，齊率衆距之，豎眼退走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Wei general Fu Shuyan invaded Nan'an; Qi led the host to resist him, and Shuyan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Wei general Fu Shuyan attacked Nan'an; Qi resisted and Shuyan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷信武將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Trusted Martial General and Administrator of the two commanderies Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he became trusted martial general and administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，葭萌人任令宗因衆之患魏也，殺魏晉壽太守，以城歸款。

translations.literal: That year, Ren Lingzong of Jiameng, because the masses resented Wei, killed the Wei Administrator of Jinshou and offered the city in submission.
translations.idiomatic: That year Ren Lingzong of Jiameng, as the people resented Wei, killed the Wei Jinshou administrator and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史鄱陽王遣齊帥衆三萬，督南梁州長史席宗範諸軍迎令宗。

translations.literal: Yizhou Inspector the Prince of Poyang sent Qi to command thirty thousand men, supervising South Liang Chief Clerk Xi Zongfan and all armies to welcome Lingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Poyang as Yizhou inspector sent Qi with thirty thousand men, overseeing chief clerk Xi Zongfan and others to welcome Lingzong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，魏東益州刺史元法僧遣子景隆來拒齊師，南安太守皇甫諶及宗範逆擊之，大破魏軍於葭萌，屠十餘城，魏將丘突、王穆等皆降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Wei East Yizhou Inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong to resist Qi's army; Nan'an Administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, smashing the Wei host at Jiameng, slaughtering more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu, Wang Mu, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Wei east Yizhou inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong against Qi; Nan'an administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, crushing the Wei army at Jiameng, sacking more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu and Wang Mu among others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 而魏更增傅豎眼兵，復來拒戰，齊兵少不利，軍引還，於是葭萌復沒於魏。

translations.literal: But Wei increased Fu Shuyan's troops and came again to resist; Qi's army was few and met with ill fortune, the army drew back, and so Jiameng again fell to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reinforced Fu Shuyan and fought again; with too few men Qi fared ill and withdrew, and Jiameng fell back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 齊在益部累年，討擊蠻獠，身無寧歲。

translations.literal: Qi spent years in the Yi region, attacking and striking Man and Liao; he himself had no peaceful year.
translations.idiomatic: Qi spent years in the Yi lands campaigning against Man and Liao; he had no peaceful year.

sentences.zh: 其居軍中，能身親勞辱，與士卒同其勤苦。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in the army he could personally share toil and hardship and suffer the same labor and pain as the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he shared labor and hardship with the troops.

sentences.zh: 自畫頓舍城壘，皆委曲得其便，調給衣糧資用，人人無所困乏。

translations.literal: He himself drew the plans for encampments and fortifications, all laid out for convenience in detail; he allocated clothing, grain, and supplies so that no man lacked what he needed.
translations.idiomatic: He sketched encampments and walls to suit every need and rationed clothing and grain so none wanted for anything.

sentences.zh: 旣爲物情所附，蠻獠亦不敢犯，是以威名行於庸、蜀。

translations.literal: Once he had won men's hearts, even Man and Liao did not dare offend him; thus his martial renown spread through Yong and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Men attached to him and even Man and Liao dared not offend him; his fame ran through Yong and Shu.

sentences.zh: 巴西郡居益州之半，又當東道沖要，刺史經過，軍府遠涉，多所窮匱。

translations.literal: Baxi commandery occupied half of Yizhou and also lay on the vital eastern route; when inspectors passed through, army offices made long forays and many were impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Baxi held half of Yizhou and lay on the vital eastern route; passing inspectors and distant army offices left many destitute.

sentences.zh: 齊沿路聚糧食，種蔬菜，行者皆取給焉。

translations.literal: Along the road Qi gathered food stores and planted vegetables; all travelers could draw their needs there.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route Qi stockpiled grain and planted vegetables so travelers could be supplied.

sentences.zh: 其能濟辦，多此類也。

translations.literal: His ability to provide and complete matters was largely of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His knack for getting things done was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷持節、都督南梁州諸軍事、智武將軍、南梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of all South Liangzhou military affairs, Sagacious Martial General, and South Liangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he became bearer of credentials, area commander of South Liang, sagacious martial general, and South Liang inspector.

sentences.zh: 普通四年，遷信武將軍、征西鄱陽王司馬、新興、永寧二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong he was transferred to Trusted Martial General, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Poyang in the Western Campaign, and Administrator of the two commanderies Xinxing and Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year four he became trusted martial general, western campaign staff officer to the prince of Poyang, and administrator of Xinxing and Yongning.

sentences.zh: 未發而卒，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Before he set out he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he died, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Palace Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made regular attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and right palace guard general.

sentences.zh: 賻錢十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: Funeral bounty: one hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral bounty was one hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 諡曰壯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Zhuang (Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：王珍國、申胄、徐元瑜、李居士，齊末咸爲列將，擁強兵，或面縛請罪，或斬關獻捷；

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Wang Zhenguo, Shen Gou, Xu Yuanyu, and Li Jushi—at the end of Qi all were ranked generals holding strong armies; some bound themselves and begged mercy, some cut the passes and presented victory;
translations.idiomatic: Chen minister of personnel Yao Cha said: Wang Zhenguo, Shen Gou, Xu Yuanyu, and Li Jushi—at the end of Qi all were ranked generals with strong armies; some bound themselves and pleaded guilt, some cut the passes and offered victory;

sentences.zh: 其能後服，馬仙琕而已。

translations.literal: Those who could submit later were only Ma Xianpin.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ma Xianpin could submit afterward.

sentences.zh: 仁義何常，蹈之則爲君子，信哉！

translations.literal: How constant are benevolence and righteousness? Tread them and one becomes a gentleman—truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness are not fixed—tread them and one becomes a gentleman. Truly!

sentences.zh: 及其臨邊撫衆，雖李牧無以加矣。

translations.literal: As for when they faced the frontier and comforted the masses, even Li Mu could add nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When they guarded the border and led the troops, even Li Mu could not surpass them.

sentences.zh: 張齊之政績，亦有異焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi's administrative achievements also had their differences.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi's achievements in office were distinctive as well.

sentences.zh: 胄、元瑜、居士入梁事迹鮮，故不爲之傳。

translations.literal: Gou, Yuanyu, and Jushi had few deeds recorded after entering Liang, so biographies were not written for them.
translations.idiomatic: Gou, Yuanyu, and Jushi left little record after entering Liang, so no biographies were written for them.

translations.idiomatic: [1] Editorial footnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
translations.idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
